texts.firmware.data_rsdk.about: The data file of Sonic Mania: everything the game is but its program. The copy that was checked is 199 MiB, a Data.rsdk as the Plus release has it. Steam's and the consoles' Data.rsdk are the same kind of file; the Plus content in it stays off, as the decompilation's licence requires. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.property.game_mode: The game's mode (0 before the game has started)
texts.property.player.class: The object's class (a number the scene gives it)
texts.property.player.is_player: The object is one of Sonic Mania's players (the fields above Character are zero when not)
texts.property.scene_time_ms: The scene timer (minutes, seconds and hundredths), in milliseconds
texts.setting.devmenu.about: Turns on the engine's developer menu (devMenu in its settings file), as the decompilation's Settings.ini does, and adds a Dev Menu control that opens it (Escape on a PC keyboard). From the menu a scene can be chosen directly. The game then also behaves as a developer's build, as it does under the decompilation with this setting: with the Plus content, for one, Z in a stage switches between Mania and Encore mode. It changes what the game does, so it is part of the project.
texts.setting.language.about: The language of the game's texts (the engine's language setting): English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (simplified) or Chinese (traditional). The game reads it, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.players.about: How many players' controls the machine has. Mania's competition mode takes up to four players with the Plus content; at 4, players 3 and 4 have controls too. It changes the inputs a movie carries, so it is part of the project.
texts.setting.plus.about: Turns on the Sonic Mania Plus content in the data file (the Plus title, Encore mode, Mighty and Ray), as owning the Plus release does. Off by default, as the decompilation's licence requires of a build given out; with it off the game is Sonic Mania without Plus. The data file must hold the Plus content (the Plus release's does). It changes the game, so a movie records it.
texts.setting.randomseed.about: The number the engine's random numbers start from. The engine takes it from the clock when it starts (time()); here it is this number, so a movie plays the same every time. The dates the game writes into its records are this number too. A movie records it.
texts.setting.region.about: The region the game believes it is in (the engine's region setting). "data" leaves it to the game's data, as upstream does by default. The game reads it (the logos it shows, for one), so a movie records it.
texts.setting.screenwidth.about: How many pixels wide the screen is (the engine's pixWidth setting). 424 is upstream's default, a 16:9 screen; 320 a 4:3 one. The width changes how far ahead the player sees and which objects are awake, so it changes the game, and a movie records it.
texts.setting.username.about: The player's name as the game shows it (username in the engine's settings file). Empty is the game's own default. Line breaks, brackets and semicolons are left out; at most 31 characters.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The files the game wrote, as Emulator > Export Save Data gave them: SaveData.bin (the save files' progress) and any other the game keeps, under their own names. They are put in place before the game starts, so the game finds them as its own.
